title: Reconnect a drive chain on two sprockets
instruction: Reconnect the open drive chain around the two sprockets. Insert the orange connecting link through both chain-end holes and secure its pins with the blue retaining plate. Leave a closed, retained loop correctly seated on both sprockets, and release both hands. The drive is unpowered.
context: Reconnect the missing link of an open chain without derailing it from either sprocket. The shafts are locked and the drive stays unpowered during this maintenance operation.
setup: A standard calibrated bimanual YAM station has a 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m nominal wood-top table (top z=0.7475 m), two parallel grippers, three calibrated cameras, a stand, lights and floor. A fixed raised aluminium service deck has top z=0.837 m and a front opening for access beneath the chain. Two locked six-tooth sprockets at (0.30,0) and (0.60,0) m have 100 mm pitch radius, 65 mm hubs and 50 x 32 x 12 mm radial teeth. Visible upper guide rims keep the chain on plane z=0.858 m; the front sprocket has a 120–240 degree service window. Eleven 100 mm-pitch printed polymer links are already routed around both sprockets, with a missing twelfth connecting link at the front: free hole centres approximately (0.2134,+/-0.05,0.858) m. Inner links weigh 50 g, outer links 80 g, and have paired 4 mm plates with 20 mm rollers, 36 mm caps and ten passive native hinges. A free orange 200 g connecting link rests on a pickup stand at (0.175,-0.32,0.873) m: backing 45 x 140 x 6 mm, two downward 10 mm pins 100 mm apart, 24 mm heads with tapered lead-ins, and a 24 x 30 x 40 mm top handle. A free blue 75 g underside keeper rests at (0.18,0.16,0.843) m: plate 80 x 128 x 12 mm, two 20 mm slots opening +x, and an extended handle. All parts have identity orientation except the authored chain links. Full primitive dimensions, nominal materials, poses and camera calibration are in setup-layout.json and scene-inventory.json.
scoring: Current-state primary score is 0 unless routing is correct: the chain forms a simple loop with winding magnitude 1 around each sprocket; all four scored pitch seats per sprocket are within 5 mm of a chain joint centre; chain height is within 4 mm of z=0.858 m and link normals have z dot >0.995. With routing correct, 0.4 requires both chain ends on their respective connector pins, within 10 mm radially and at connector-local z strictly between -22 and -10 mm. 0.7 additionally requires the keeper above both pin heads, at connector-local z between -40 and -30 mm, relative orientation at most 0.10 rad, and both stems inside its actual fork slots. Full score 1 additionally requires both stems near the closed slot ends, connector within 8 mm and 0.10 rad of its installed pose, every moving body below 20 mm/s and 0.3 rad/s, both grippers open >=70 mm, and whole-robot clearance >=25 mm for at least 1 s. Any moving solid escaping x=[-0.19,0.91], y=[-0.65,0.65], z>=0.7415 m or becoming nonfinite permanently forces zero. README and scoring.py give exact slot bounds.
reset_notes: Restore all free parts and ten hinge positions to the listed fixed layout, open both grippers at ready, settle 0.5 s, then begin scoring. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Native rigid contact and ten passive chain hinges. Dual chain plates leave physical space for the sprocket teeth. Connector pins pass down through the two end holes; the separate fork keeper slides into their stems above the heads. Guide rims and the deck retain routing without task-body writes, attachments or software latches. This is an enlarged unpowered training drive with locked shafts and a custom friction-retained connecting link; there is no elasticity, fracture, wear, powered torque-transmission, rated-load or vibration-locking test.
scores: Revised scripted demo: 1.0; revised Dream-1 evaluation: pending. Previous joint-only media do not validate this revision.
